column1: # How much stack the Lean kernel needs to build each prelude.
# profile<TAB>prelude<TAB>budget_bytes
# Each number is the SMALLEST POWER OF TWO on which
# `examples/kernel_stack_envelope` completes that prelude's build, found by
# bisection with `scripts/check-kernel-stack-envelope.sh --measure`. It is a
# measured requirement, not a preference: one power of two below each row, the
# build aborts with SIGABRT (exit 134), and `--check` re-demonstrates that on
# every run so a green result is never vacuous.
# Measured 2026-08-26 on s4 (rustc via the repo's default toolchain);
# the two `creal` rows re-measured 2026-08-28, same host. `integer`, `cpoint`
# and `complex` re-measured 2026-08-29, same host, after `just check`'s
# stack-envelope step went red on all three.
# ## What these numbers say
# * 2026-08-29: `integer`, `cpoint`, `complex` all outgrew their pinned
#   RELEASE budget; all three re-measured by `--measure` to a passing power
#   of two (no divergent term found for any of them). Growth was NOT
#   uniform, which refutes the standing hypothesis that `nat`'s same-day
#   bitwise-family growth (`Nat.Pair`, `Nat.binaryRec`, `land`/`lor`/`ldiff`
#   plus their comm/assoc/`*_bit` lemmas) drove all three as downstream
#   consumers -- `nat`'s own release row is UNCHANGED at 65536, and the
#   three consumers grew at wildly different rates:
#     release integer   65536 ->    131072   ( 2x)
#     release cpoint   1048576 ->  8388608   ( 8x)
#     release complex   262144 ->  8388608   (32x)
#   Each prelude's own recent history explains its own rate far better than
#   a shared upstream cause: `int_prelude.rs`/`int_prelude/` picked up
#   incremental, modest lemmas (`Int.gcd_div`, `Int.fib_two_mul`,
#   `Int.emod_natAbs_bound`) -- consistent with the smallest, 2x, growth.
#   `creal_point.rs` (the `cpoint` prelude) picked up a run of Euclidean
#   geometry identities carried "squared throughout" to avoid a square root
#   (Heron's formula, Menelaus, Ceva, the Euler line, Cauchy-Schwarz,
#   circumcentre/radical-axis constructions) -- large algebraic terms, 8x.
#   `complex.rs` picked up the polynomial/factor-theorem family
#   (`Complex.polyMul`, `hornerFromTop`/`factorQuotient`, the FTA-approx
#   groundwork) plus the modulus triangle inequality -- the heaviest
#   additions of the three, and the 32x row to match. So: attribute growth
#   to each prelude's OWN recent commits, not to a shared upstream driver.
#   DEBUG was checked too, since the pin file carries debug rows for all
#   three, and it did NOT move in lockstep with release:
#     debug   integer   262144    -> unchanged (confirmed by --measure)
#     debug   cpoint  33554432    -> unchanged (confirmed by direct probe:
#                                    passes at 33554432, fails at 16777216 --
#                                    same bisection result as before)
#     debug   complex   4194304   ->  16777216  (4x; the old pin now FAILS)
#   `cpoint`'s debug/release ratio therefore fell from the previously-quoted
#   32x to 4x (33,554,432 / 8,388,608) -- a further illustration, on top of
#   the existing entry below, that the debug/release ratio is per-term and
#   was never a constant to calibrate once.
#   Judgment call, stated explicitly: `nat`, `rat` and `creal`'s release
#   rows all currently print "margin < 2x below pin" (build at the pin,
#   abort at half). None of the three FAILED at their pin, so none are
#   raised here -- raising a passing row is a separate, discretionary
#   change, and `nat_prelude/` and `creal/` are explicitly other lanes'
#   files this session. If one of those rows goes red, re-derive it the
#   same way: `--measure --profile release --prelude <name>`.
#   RAISED 2026-08-28 (8x and 64x). Re-measured twice, independently, by
#   `--measure` in both profiles after a lane reported the release row red.
#   What grew: two days of `CReal` development -- EVT row 2 and the closure of
#   its labeled gap, supOn rungs 1-6 including the multi-level nearest-point
#   lemma, pi rungs 2-3, and the integral family. No single declaration did it;
#   the prelude simply got much bigger.
#   The symptom was NOT a kernel bug and NOT a non-terminating term. It was
#   `reconstruct::arithmetic::monomial_bound` aborting with SIGABRT, because
#   `LraReconstructCtx::try_new_over_constructed_reals_reporting` builds the
#   `CReal` prelude on the CALLING thread -- and a `#[test]` thread gets 2 MiB.
#   An overflow aborts the process, so only the FIRST constructed-reals test to
#   run gets named; `zero_product`, `product_positivstellensatz`,
#   `signature_tests` and `reconstruct::tests` were affected too and reported
#   nothing. That constructor now builds on a 256 MiB worker thread.
#   READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING THE `--release` DISCRIMINATOR. CLAUDE.md's rule
#   is that a stack overflow surviving `--release` means runaway recursion
#   rather than a margin overrun. This case FAILED in release and was still a
#   finite, bounded requirement -- it had simply grown past the default in BOTH
#   profiles. The rule separates a debug-only margin problem from everything
#   else; it does not separate a grown requirement from a divergent term. Only
#   `--measure` does: a real requirement bisects to a passing power of two.
#   PRIOR NOTE, kept because the mechanism recurs: `creal` DEBUG used to need
#   exactly 2,097,152 -- precisely the default a spawned thread gets, so there
#   was no margin at all. `CReal.e` landing is what pushed it over then, and the
#   symptom was `every_creal_declaration_is_checked_and_axiom_free` -- the guard
#   behind this project's axiom-freedom claim -- silently aborting rather than
#   running.
# * `cpoint` in a DEBUG build needs 33,554,432 bytes. The `on_a_deep_stack`
#   copies that covered it used 64 MiB, so the real headroom was 2x, not the
#   comfortable margin the number suggests. `DEEP_STACK_BYTES` is 256 MiB, which
#   is 8x this row.
# * Debug costs up to 32x release for the same term (cpoint: 33,554,432 vs
#   1,048,576, as measured 2026-08-26). That ratio is why
#   `prelude_theorem_inventory` must be run `--release`, and it is the
#   measured reason a single recursion-DEPTH limit cannot be calibrated
#   once: the same term fits in one profile and not the other while its
#   depth is identical.
#   STALE AS OF 2026-08-29: `cpoint`'s release row moved to 8,388,608 (see
#   above), so the CURRENT ratio for `cpoint` is 4x (33,554,432 /
#   8,388,608), not 32x. The 32x FIGURE is kept as the historical
#   measurement that motivated the `--release` rule; it is not this row's
#   ratio anymore. The rule itself (debug/release ratio is per-term, not a
#   constant) is reinforced, not weakened, by the ratio itself having moved.
# * 2026-09-03: `rat` outgrew its pinned budget in BOTH profiles and the
#   `--check` gate was RED on `main` -- found by a lane chasing an unrelated
#   debug abort, not by anyone running the gate, which is the same way the
#   2026-08-28 `creal` row was found. Both re-derived by `--measure`, so
#   neither is a divergent term:
#   What grew: 84 commits touched `rat_prelude/` between 2026-08-29 and
#   2026-09-03 -- the determinant family through to multiplicativity at
#   symbolic `n` (ADR-1440, ADR-1543), `Rat.prodRange`/`Rat.sumMaps`, the
#   row-echelon form and the pivot/sweep obligations (ADR-1554), and
#   `Rat.rank` with the row-rank = column-rank bridge (ADR-1562). No single
#   declaration did it; per this file's own rule, the attribution is to this
#   prelude's OWN recent commits and not to a shared upstream cause.
#   AND `rat` WAS NOT THE ONLY RED ROW. Running the FULL `--check` in both
#   profiles on the same day found four more, none of which anyone had seen,
#   all re-derived by `--measure` (so none is a divergent term):
#     debug   integer   262144 ->   524288  (2x)
#   `DEEP_STACK_BYTES` (256 MiB) is still 4x the new `cpoint` debug row, so
#   `on_a_deep_stack` call sites keep their headroom. The lesson is the one
#   the 2026-08-28 entry already recorded and which held again here: nobody
#   runs `--check`, so it goes red silently and is found by whoever trips
#   over an abort. Growth is ordinary; an unexplained row is the defect.
#   THE DEBUG ROW IS NOW EXACTLY THE 2 MiB A SPAWNED THREAD GETS, so every
#   `#[test]` that calls `build_rat_prelude` on its own thread has zero
#   margin -- the same shape that let one `creal` declaration silently stop
#   the axiom-freedom guard from running (see the 2026-08-28 entry below).
#   `cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib` in debug is green today at
#   1,498 tests, but the next `rat` declaration of any depth will abort
#   something, and the abort will name only the first casualty.
# ## When a row goes red

# Re-derive it (`--measure --profile

--prelude `), raise the row, and
# say in the commit what grew. A rising row is not a defect; an unexplained one
# is.
# `logic`, `axreal` and `string` have RELEASE rows deliberately omitted: their
# release builds complete on 8 KiB, the smallest stack the bisection probes, so
# a pinned budget for them could not be shown to fail and would report a
# permanent WARN. They keep their debug rows, where they need 128-256 KiB.
